_note: The <cli> document corpus — the FIFTH node (cli-authoring.md). A command-line program is a .dsx document: the head declares what the program may reach (env names, executables, filesystem roots) plus the <action> bodies, and the body declares the command surface, because the structure of a CLI is its command surface exactly as the structure of a server is its route surface. These cases define PARSING and the closed vocabulary; dispatch.json defines argv binding and seams.json defines what a body may reach. Platform-neutral by construction: a case is (source, expected-table) or (source, expected-abort), so a Kotlin or Swift CLI host implements against the same file. `abort` cases assert the MESSAGE FRAGMENT and the LINE, because a build that half-works because a typo'd attribute was ignored is the silent class these gates exist to make impossible — and on a CLI the attribute in question is usually `action` or `handler`, which decides whether author code runs at all.

cases.name: minimal-document
cases.source:
<cli as="tool" version="1.0.0" summary="a tool">
  <head>
    <action as="greet">
      return { code: 0 }
    </action>
  </head>
  <command as="greet" action="greet" summary="say hello"/>
</cli>

cases.name: declares-env-exec-and-roots
cases.source:
<cli as="tool" version="1.0.0">
  <head>
    <env as="HOME"/>
    <env as="CI"/>
    <exec as="git"/>
    <root as="project" path="."/>
    <action as="noop">return 0</action>
  </head>
  <command as="noop" action="noop"/>
</cli>

cases.name: command-declares-flags-and-positionals
cases.source:
<cli as="tool" version="1.0.0">
  <head>
    <action as="run">return 0</action>
  </head>
  <command as="run" action="run" summary="run it">
    <flag as="project" type="string" summary="project root"/>
    <flag as="strict" type="boolean" summary="warnings fail too"/>
    <flag as="package" type="string" repeatable="true"/>
    <positional as="files" variadic="true" summary="files to read"/>
  </command>
</cli>

cases.name: a-command-may-eject-to-a-named-host-handler
cases._why: The server's TypeScript ejection hatch, applied here. A CLI that shells out, streams a build, or drives a watcher wants a real host function; the point of the document is that such a command is still DECLARED, so --help, the command table and the argument contract stay in one place even when the body is not markup.

cases.name: an-action-body-is-raw-text-and-keeps-its-operators
cases._why: A body is JSE, and JSE contains <, > and &&. An XML parser must reject those or silently mangle them, so action content is read as RAW TEXT to its closing tag — the same rule lint_dsx.rb applies. This case exists because mangling here is silent: the body still parses, it just means something else. The command declares a and b because `inputs=` is a checked contract: an action may only name arguments its command actually offers.
cases.source:
<cli as="tool" version="1.0.0">
  <head>
    <action as="cmp" inputs="a, b">
      if (a < b && b > 0) { return 0 }
      return 1
    </action>
  </head>
  <command as="cmp" action="cmp">
    <flag as="a" type="string"/>
    <flag as="b" type="string"/>
  </command>
</cli>

cases.name: reject-command-with-neither-action-nor-handler
cases._why: A command that names no implementation is the one shape that looks complete and does nothing.

cases.name: reject-a-non-final-variadic-positional
cases._why: A variadic that is not last silently swallows the arguments meant for the ones after it.
cases.source:
<cli as="tool" version="1.0.0">
  <head>
    <action as="x">return 0</action>
  </head>
  <command as="x" action="x">
    <positional as="files" variadic="true"/>
    <positional as="target"/>
  </command>
</cli>

cases.name: reject-a-reserved-command-name
cases._why: help and version are answered by the host from the document itself, so a command claiming either would be shadowed and never run.

cases.name: reject-an-input-the-command-does-not-offer
cases._why: A body reads its arguments by bare name, so a typo in inputs= does not fail — the name is simply absent and every branch reading it takes the empty path. Pinning the list against the command's own flags and positionals turns that silence into a build error.
cases.source:
<cli as="tool" version="1.0.0">
  <head>
    <action as="run" inputs="projekt">return 0</action>
  </head>
  <command as="run" action="run">
    <flag as="project" type="string"/>
  </command>
</cli>
